title: Detect and triage gradual usage/cost/latency drift
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Objective:
Implement a production-grade detector and triage flow for gradual drift in usage, cost, and latency signals. Existing alerting focuses on sharp spikes and multivariate outliers; this ticket targets slow but sustained deviations (weeks to months) that cause cost creep, SLA erosion, or capacity surprises.

Background:
- Several accounts have shown slowly increasing tail latency and quietly rising per-request cost over the past quarters. These are often due to model changes, routing policy shifts, or client-side SDK changes.
- Current anomaly pipeline flags large deviations but returns many false positives for regular seasonal patterns. We need a noise-resistant, explainable drift detector with automated triage suggestions.

Goals:
1) Detect sustained upward/downward trends at per-customer, per-route, and per-model granularity with seasonality-aware baselines.
2) Produce an anomaly score and an explainability payload (top contributing dimensions: route, model, region, instance type).
3) Suppress transient noise and avoid alert fatigue: group related findings and apply progressive notification (Slack summary -> Pager only if impact crosses SLA/cost thresholds).
4) Integrate results into Console: issue timeline, suggested playbook steps, and auto-created investigation tickets for high-impact drifts.

Approach (high level):
- Signal definition: derive three canonical time series per scope (count-normalized latency p95, per-call cost USD, request volume). Add enrichment dimensions: customer_tier, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private), region, model_family.
- Baseline algorithm: use seasonal decomposition (STL) to remove weekly pattern, followed by EWMA on residuals to detect persistent shift. We will also compute a linear trend fit (slope) over multiple windows (7d, 28d, 90d) and normalize by historical variance to form a unitless drift score.
- Streaming vs batch: implement streaming detection in the Flink pipeline for near-real-time detection of fast drifts (7–14 days), and a periodic batch job (daily) for long-term 28–90 day drift aggregation and scoring.
- Explainability: when a drift score crosses thresholds, compute per-dimension conditional deltas (e.g., delta latency for model_variant=X vs others) to rank contributors.
- Grouping and suppression: group anomalies by fingerprint (customer + route + model family) and suppress repeated alerts for the same fingerprint unless score increases by >50%.

Pipeline changes required:
1) Ingest enrichment fields into analytics topic: allocation_id, model_variant, route_name, deployment_mode (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/212).
2) Add a "drift_baselines" continuous materialized view (Materialize / Timescale) that stores STL seasonal component and EWMA residual for each scope.
3) New Flink job: drift-detector-v1 (k8s job spec in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/data-pipeline/tree/main/jobs/drift-detector).
4) Alert writer: extend notify-service to accept drift findings with a structured payload (score, trend_direction, top_contributors, evidence window).

Alerting and triage workflow:
- Low-impact drift: create Console banner + PRD link recommended, assigned to the customer success owner. No Pager.
- Medium-impact: Slack channel summary, create investigation ticket (prefill query and candidate contributing dimensions).
- High-impact (cost > $X/day delta or tail latency breaches SLA for >72h): Pager to on-call infra and auto-create high-priority incident board card.

Operational considerations:
- False positive budget: aim for <1 false high-impact pager per quarter correlated across customers.
- Storage: baseline windows will retain 365 days; we will compress daily aggregates for older ranges.
- Backfill: initial run will backfill 180 days to establish baselines; backfill runbook included in links.

Instrumentation / Queries (examples):
- Compute normalized p95: SELECT customer_id, route, model_family, date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hour, percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) / NULLIF(requests,0) AS p95_norm FROM usage_events WHERE ts >= now() - interval '90 days' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4;
- Trend slope regression: -- pseudocode: compute slope of p95_norm over 28d using linear regression on hourly buckets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Drift detector emits findings to staging topic with score and contributors for >95% of active customers during 28d evaluation run.
- False positive rate on historical labeled dataset below 12% for medium alerts, below 3% for high alerts.
- Console shows grouped drift cards with contributor breakdown and links to investigation queries.
- On-call receives high-impact pager only when thresholds defined in the playbook are exceeded.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: STL + EWMA + regression is more computationally heavy than simple z-score. We'll mitigate by aggregating hourly and limiting cardinality (only compute per-customer for >threshold usage).
- Explainability vs recall: detailed contributor attribution may miss subtle multi-factor drifts; we'll prioritize precision for Pager-level alerts and allow broader suggestions for low/medium findings.

Next steps / Implementation tasks:
- [ENG] Add enrichment fields to ingestion (PR open).
- [ENG] Implement baseline materialized view schema and retention policy.
- [ENG] Build Flink job and local test harness (unit tests + integration tests against sample dataset).
- [PM/DX] Draft Console UI for drift cards and triage modal (link to design brief).
- [SRE] Define pager thresholds and runbook.

Deliverables:
- drift-detector-v1 streaming job + batch aggregator.
- API contract for notify-service drift payload.
- Console drift card UI and investigation ticket template.
- Playbook with thresholds and suppression rules.

steps: Merge ingestion PR and deploy to staging
Deploy drift-detector Flink job to staging and validate against synthetic scenarios
Hook notify-service to accept drift payloads and write to staging findings topic
Implement Console UI for grouped drift cards in staging
Run 28-day live validation and compare against historical labeled anomalies
Gradual rollout: 10% of customers -> 33% -> 100% across 3 waves
acceptance_criteria: Staging drift topic has structured findings for 95% of active test customers
False positive rates within targets on labeled dataset
Console shows contributor breakdown and links to investigation query
Pager only triggers after 72h confirmation window for high-impact drifts
rollout_plan: Wave 1: 10% pilot customers with high usage (monitor metrics and adjust suppression) - 2 weeks
Wave 2: 33% expansion and runbook dry-run with SRE and CS - 2 weeks
Wave 3: full rollout with automated ticket creation enabled - 1 week
